D.label: DARK ROOM
D.name: Dark-room curtain
D.text: The heavy curtain to the dark room. Scintillations are faint, so the experiment is watched in the dark.

X.label: FOIL APPARATUS
X.name: Foil apparatus
X.text: The scattering apparatus: radon source, lead slit, gold foil in a vacuum chamber, a zinc-sulfide screen and a microscope.

Z.label: BOARD
Z.name: Chalkboard
Z.text: Chalkboard: 'Geiger and Marsden, 1909. Alpha particles from radon. Do any come back?' Underneath, in Rutherford's hand: 'Almost as incredible as if you fired a 15-inch shell at a piece of tissue paper and it came back and hit you.'

S.label: RADON
S.name: Radon source in lead
S.text: A sealed glass tube of radon gas inside a lead block. Its decay products (radium C) throw out alpha particles at about 7.7 MeV. A narrow slit lets a thin beam out.

P.label: PUMP
P.name: Vacuum pump
P.text: The vacuum pump. Air would scatter and stop alpha particles, so the chamber is pumped empty.

V.label: GLASSWORK
V.name: Glassware and valves
V.text: Spare glass tubing, stopcocks and a jar of mercury for the pump. Everything is hand-made.

G.label: GOLD LEAF
G.name: Gold leaf
G.text: Gold beaten to leaf about 0.0004 mm thick: only a few thousand atoms. It is the thinnest metal sheet anyone can make.

M.label: LOG BOOK
M.name: Counting log book
M.text: The log book. Marsden counted flashes on the screen by eye, one at a time, for hours in the dark, and wrote each count here.

N.label: NOTICE
N.name: Notice board
N.text: Physical Laboratories, Victoria University of Manchester. 'Silence while counting.'

T.label: TEA
T.name: Tea tray
T.text: Tea. The team started most days with it, and stopped counting only because their eyes gave out.
